coverage_claim: Reviewable-draft coverage for Jurisdiction as a bounded competence: identity and territorial coding, authority-holder and conferral, the four scope axes with declared power type, inter-jurisdictional relations and exceptions, lifecycle with provenance and contestation, and identifier interoperability — 6 bundles, 13 layers, 28 findings, 113 questions, 10 artifacts and 11 functions, with every layer resting on at least one tier-1 primary source. Coverage is EU- and UN-instrument-weighted and audited by one provider only; it is not complete for any national legal system, and non-State legal orders, arbitral competence, cross-border data-access regimes, State-succession instruments and outer space, Antarctic and deep-seabed regimes remain declared or newly identified omissions.

boundary_decision.rationale: Two axes must not be conflated. On the record plane the frozen registry value standalone-mm says only that vr.wm-pol-015 is registered as a free-standing meta-model record with empty contains_ids and a single parent WM-PLC-004; it classifies the registration, not the subject, and is not a member of the subject-model enum. On the subject plane the most defensible schema kind is entity, and the declared value is accepted. The decisive test is identity independence: the jurisdiction identifier is permanently stable, never renamed or reassigned, survives reorganisation, renaming or abolition of the authority-holder (q-holder-continuity), survives extension, reduction, cession, merger and split (q-change-identifier), and on extinction is retired by obsolescence marker plus successor link rather than deleted. 'relationship' was seriously considered because the purpose binds a holder to a competence, but a reified relationship loses identity when an endpoint changes, which this model expressly forbids. 'aggregate' was considered because the record roots dependent collections (alignments, crosswalks, exception entries, attestations, tombstone), but those are attributes of a single record rather than independently registered sibling models, and contains_ids is empty. 'classifier' fits only the subordinate typology code list, not the subject. Status is accepted rather than reclassified, but the registry review_state boundary-review-required must stay open until the authority-holder cardinality rule and the per-power-type scope asymmetry recorded below are settled.

decisions.concept: Subject-model entry kind: entity versus reified relationship
decisions.rationale: The identifier persists across change of authority-holder and change of territory, which a reified holder-to-scope relationship could not do; identity independence from both endpoints is the entity test and the model enforces it explicitly.

decisions.disposition: accepted with a mandatory cardinality rule to be added
decisions.rationale: The purpose statement binds 'an identified authority-holder' (singular) while q-holder-plurality asks how several bodies sharing one scope record their distinct share. The root must be pinned as one record per holder-competence-scope tuple, with shared scope expressed through concurrency relations rather than multi-holder records.

decisions.concept: Per-power-type scope asymmetry (prescriptive reach exceeding enforcement reach)
decisions.disposition: deferred — blocking for candidate-to-accepted promotion, not for draft publication
decisions.rationale: q-power-asymmetry requires the asymmetry to be recorded rather than smoothed, but the four scope axes attach once per record, so the model's own GDPR counterexample cannot be instantiated without either scoping the axes per power type or splitting the record. The structural choice must be resolved by review before promotion.

decisions.concept: Deposited chart and coordinate-list artifact versus the no-geometry out-of-scope rule
decisions.disposition: reclassified to a citation-and-digest evidence record
decisions.rationale: media_or_form for deposited-coordinate-record lists 'nautical chart' and 'list of geographical coordinates', which reads as holding the very boundary material the out-of-scope list and the reference-over-replication policy assign to the spatial model and the depositary; only the notification reference, depositary, instant and digest should be held here.

decisions.concept: serial_naming_rule claim that AGENTS.md is the sole non-serial artifact
decisions.disposition: rejected as written; correction required before publication
decisions.rationale: Two artifacts declare serial:false — agents-bootstrap-descriptor and jurisdiction-typology-code-list — so the artifact identity rule contradicts the structure it governs. The code list is also version-governed with deprecation, so its serial flag and the rule text must be reconciled.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist assertion of eleven composition links
decisions.rationale: The frozen relationship contract is empty and the payload contains nine boundary notes and zero composition links. The ownership dimension must be restated as nine boundary notes plus named placeholder composition targets under the registry_links placeholder rule, or the count must be evidenced.

decisions.concept: Source support for State succession, cession and dissolution
decisions.disposition: accepted as declared-only; the grounding claim is struck
decisions.rationale: scope-change-succession-and-dissolution cites SRC-003, SRC-009, SRC-012 and SRC-014, none of which governs State succession; SRC-014 is the immunities convention. The lifecycle checklist note claiming succession grounding overstates the evidence and must be downgraded pending a succession instrument.

decisions.concept: urn:lex Internet-Draft as grounding for permanent identifier stability
decisions.rationale: SRC-009 is draft-spinosa-urn-lex-24, a non-consensus expiring Internet-Draft carried at authority tier 2, yet it alone carries a hard compatibility rule and a stated divergence from national code-reuse practice. The rule should also rest on ELI and ECLI persistence practice or be marked as a local policy choice.

decisions.concept: ISO 3166 held at identity tier 2 while NUTS and M49 are alignment-only
decisions.disposition: accepted with the unverified-source marker retained
decisions.rationale: The asymmetry is defensible because ISO codes are the tokens that Akoma Ntoso and urn:lex actually govern, whereas NUTS and M49 are statistical, but iso.org returned HTTP 403 so the ISO wording is unverified and every structural claim resting solely on it must stay flagged.

decisions.concept: SRC-019 (gdpr-info.eu) as a tier-3 non-primary reproduction
decisions.disposition: accepted as a non-sole supporting citation
decisions.rationale: Both findings that cite it (power-type-classification, extraterritorial-reach-and-connecting-factors) also cite SRC-016, the CELEX text, so it never carries an assertion alone; it must be marked secondary in provenance and must not become sole support in any revision.

decisions.concept: Tombstone register exemption from retention disposition
decisions.disposition: accepted with an explicit non-disposable rule required
decisions.rationale: Retention classes impose a minimum period, which read literally could authorise disposing of the append-only tombstone register and so break the identifier non-reuse guarantee and the resolution of historical ELI, ECLI and urn:lex citations; the register must be declared permanently non-disposable.

decisions.concept: Rome Statute pinned at the 1998 corrected text
decisions.disposition: accepted with a version-pin correction required
decisions.rationale: SRC-007 pins A/CONF.183/9 as adopted, which does not carry subsequently adopted amendments; the subject-matter competence catalogue and the temporal-reach claims should cite the current consolidated Statute so that catalogue versioning ties to amending instruments as q-matter-versioning demands.

decisions.concept: Missing operations for competing claims and access restrictions
decisions.disposition: deferred; no function additions permitted in single-provider mode
decisions.rationale: crud.create requires competing claims to be recorded and access.exceptions require a named approver, reason and scheduled review instant, but no declared function adds a competing claim to an existing record or registers and reviews a restriction. Raised for the next revision because add_functions must remain empty under the waiver contract.

decisions.concept: Access scopes applied to record instances
decisions.rationale: bundle, layer, finding and artifact are context-structure scopes, yet the exceptions restrict record instances and fields such as embargoed coordinate deposits and draft scope changes; a record-and-field scope must be named so instance-level restriction is expressible without stretching the context scopes.

publication_holds: Live source and version verification is outstanding: no URL, HTTP status or version pin in the nineteen-source set was re-fetched during this audit. ISO 3166-1/-2 is admittedly unretrieved (HTTP 403), SRC-009 is an expiring Internet-Draft, SRC-007 is pinned to the 1998 corrected Rome Statute text, SRC-012 to the 2024-01-01 NUTS consolidation, SRC-015 to NAL version 20260617-0, and the UNCLOS Part II and Part V URLs are legacy paths. Every pin must be revalidated with a retrieval instant and digest before the draft leaves reviewable state.

The owner-authorized absence of independent second-provider review must be visible in every published artifact: Grok was waived by the repository owner on 2026-08-29T09:06:27Z after repeated structured-output failures, so this result carries one provider plus a no-tools adversarial audit only, has no cross-provider agreement on entry kind, sources or structure, and remains a reviewable draft rather than a validated model.

The frozen registry record stays at status candidate with review_state boundary-review-required and an empty relations_ref, and the relationship contract is empty. Composition targets (spatial, legislation, case-law, entity-registry, conflict-of-laws and policy-decision/enforcement runtime models) must be published as named placeholders with intended relation types so the ownership contract is auditable before the sibling models exist.

Two artifact-identity defects must be corrected before publication: the serial_naming_rule asserts a single non-serial artifact while two are declared non-serial, and the deposited chart and coordinate-list artifact must be reduced to a citation-and-digest evidence record so it does not hold geometry the model declares out of scope.

The coverage checklist must be corrected where it overstates evidence: the claim of eleven composition links is unsupported by the frozen contract, and the State-succession grounding claim is unsupported by any cited source.
deferred_research: Retrieve ISO 3166-1 and ISO 3166-2 through the ISO Online Browsing Platform and re-ground every structural claim currently resting on indirect citation through Akoma Ntoso, urn:lex, UNSD and the EU Countries NAL.

Obtain a retrievable authoritative statement of the prescriptive/adjudicative/enforcement trichotomy (ILC A/61/10 annex or an equivalent doctrinal source) so power-type classification is no longer supported only by the operative structure of Brussels Ia, GDPR Article 3 and the immunities convention.

Add the HCCH 2019 Judgments Convention to the source set; recognition and refusal grounds currently rest on Brussels Ia and the 2005 Choice of Court Convention alone, which leaves recognition outside chosen-court cases unevidenced.
Consult the 1978 and 1983 Vienna Conventions on Succession of States, or an equivalent authority, to ground succession, cession and dissolution, which no cited source currently governs.

Consult the Vienna Conventions on Diplomatic Relations (1961) and Consular Relations (1963) so that privilege and immunity are not modelled solely from the 2004 State immunity convention, which is itself not universally in force.

Verify the current status of draft-spinosa-urn-lex (expiry, successor draft or RFC), the current NUTS consolidation after the triennial amendment cadence, and the current EU Countries and territories NAL version, and repin all three.

Consult UNCLOS Part XI, the Antarctic Treaty regime and the Outer Space Treaty to decide whether non-territorial competence regimes need dedicated structure or can be carried by the existing typology and functional-competence elements.

Determine whether consensual competence should be extended to arbitral seat, kompetenz-kompetenz and award enforcement by consulting the New York Convention and ICSID regime, or whether that scope belongs to a sibling model.
